source.title: Error Sensitivity Modulation based Experience Replay: Mitigating Abrupt Representation Drift in Continual Learning
source.authors: Fahad Sarfraz; E. Arani; Bahram Zonooz

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates noisy-label learning in continual learning and tracks model performance on clean and noisy samples during training, extending the setting relevant to V6.
record.gate_note: The noisy-label benchmark and ablation results report continual-learning performance, not whether models fit completely random labels, achieve chance test error, or retain perfect training fit as noise increases. Figure 3a tracks clean/noisy sample accuracy during training; Figure 3b measures noisy-label percentage in the memory buffer, which does not directly measure the claimed model behavior.
record.test_reason: Figures 3(a) and S3 track clean- and noisy-label accuracy over training in continual learning, directly bearing on V6. However, the supplied text preserves no readable curves or explicit clean-before-noisy ordering, so no directional verdict is justified.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the noisy-label experiments. The broader conclusion is that ESMER mitigates abrupt representation drift, improves robustness to noisy labels, and produces more uniform performance across continual-learning tasks.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes error-sensitivity modulation with experience replay for continual learning; it does not reproduce the random-label fitting experiments in the original sources.

fits_no_version.finding: ESMER reduces noisy-label memorization relative to ER and improves continual-learning test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Error sensitivity modulation and a stable model can reduce noisy-label memorization in continual learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Error-sensitive reservoir sampling reduces the proportion of noisy labels in episodic memory.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selecting low-loss samples improves replay-buffer label quality.

record.problems: The clean/noisy accuracy trajectories are presented in a figure without textual ordering or exact values. The study evaluates symmetric label noise in a continual-learning setting, not completely random labels on the full training set.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results directly measure V1–V5. Noisy-label benchmark accuracy and component ablations in Tables 3–4 measure continual-learning performance rather than the random-label fitting behaviors those versions specify. Figure 3(b) reports noisy-label percentage in the buffer, not model fitting or memorization.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and fitting with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time ratios for true versus random labels and convergence slowing with increasing corruption.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout a corruption sweep reaching completely random labels, with test error approaching chance.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting and whether removing them preserves true-label generalization.
The trajectories do not separately identify learning shared patterns versus memorizing individual examples; completely random-label training is not evaluated.

record.verdict_notes: Neither reduced memorization under mitigation nor declining test accuracy with increasing noise establishes V6's learning order or V4's perfect training fit. Figure S3 is already declared in the record, so its working-model comparison is not an undeclared missing result.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment trains on completely random labels and tests training error, chance-level test error, or unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed across label corruption levels.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment.
No sweep from clean to completely random labels measuring perfect training fit and test error.
No experiment testing weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation as barriers to fitting random labels or as determinants of true-label generalization.

The study tracks clean- and noisy-sample accuracy over training, but the supplied text does not state whether shared real-label patterns are learned before noisy labels are memorized; the result is shown in a figure without a textual ordering.
